data.answer: Restores are tested every quarter. The most recent restore test was on 12 September 2026 and was completed in 2 hours 40 minutes, within the 4-hour RTO.

Nimbus Labs uses 9 sub-processors that may process customer data, including AWS and an email delivery provider. The current list is shared with customers on request, and customers receive 30 days' advance notice before a new sub-processor is added.
Tier 1 vendors are reviewed once a year, Tier 2 vendors are reviewed every two years, and any vendor that suffers a security incident is reviewed immediately.
Yes, a background check (identity, employment history and education) is completed before the start date for every employee, intern and contractor.
All access is revoked within 4 hours of the person's exit time.
No. Customer data is stored in India by default (AWS Mumbai), but disaster recovery copies are held in Singapore.

The provided knowledge chunks only mention the notification commitment for when a breach involving customer data is confirmed (within 72 hours), but do not specify the notification commitment for a suspected, not yet confirmed, security incident.
The provided knowledge chunks detail encryption at rest and field-level encryption for sensitive fields, but do not mention encrypting data while it is in use (such as confidential computing).

The provided chunks include incident acknowledgment timeframes by severity level (P1: 15 minutes, P2: 1 hour, P3: 1 business day, P4: 3 business days), but do not explicitly detail general contractual support hours.
